encode_chunked.note: b58encode_int peels five digits per big-integer divmod (base**5 fits one internal int digit, so each division costs the same as a division by base) and builds the output in a bytearray instead of prepending to bytes.

decode_chunked.note: b58decode_int accumulates five digits in a small int and folds them into the big integer with one multiply-add, so the number of big-integer operations drops five-fold. Submitted on the long-blob target: on address-sized strings (decode_ir) the per-call work dominates and the same change measured 0.9935, under the 1% minimum.

encode_long_chunked.note: The same change as encode_chunked, submitted on the long-blob target: five digits per big-integer division and a bytearray instead of prepending to bytes.
